messages:
maria: quick heads-up — I see dev-token-qa (dev-token scope=chat) suddenly allowed /v1/embeddings calls this morning around 02:12 UTC. Likely correlated with last night's KMS rewrap. Not sure if it's a cache or scope-check fallback.

raj: can you paste a sample log line and the exact token id?

maria: log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T02:12:03Z] svc=auth decision=allow token_id=tok_dev_qa01 scopes=[chat] route=/v1/embeddings auth_check=scope_cache hit ttl=7200 fallback=none
```
token masked in logs as tok_dev_qa01. Notice scope listed as [chat] but route=/v1/embeddings. decision=allow and auth_check shows cache hit.

sam: so scope_cache hit is probably returning a cached allow record from before we tightened embeddings vs chat policy. Did we change per-route tagging in the recent authz refactor?

elaine: yes — yesterday's rollout added per-route tags but also changed the cache tag key to include kms-keytag. If the rewrap changed keytag, old cache entries should have been invalidated, but looks like TTL kept old entries live.

raj: reproduction steps I ran:
1) mint a dev-token with only chat scope
2) call POST /v1/embeddings with Authorization: Bearer <token>
3) see 200 and model returns embeddings

curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_dev_qa01"
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

maria: exact failure mode: the cache entry used a legacy cache key that doesn't include the new kms keytag. After rewrap, KMS tag changed, but our cache layer falls back to tagless lookup for a short window (optimizes for availability). That fallback path wasn't strictly validating per-route scopes.

ops-bot: automated alert — authz.cache.fallback_rate increased by 8x between 2026-03-18T02:00Z and 2026-03-18T02:20Z.

tony: omg — so during rewrap we basically allowed some tokens to be treated as if they had route-level allowlists? How many tokens affected?

elaine: preliminary query: running an audit search for entries where decision=allow AND route!=scope AND auth_check=fallback OR cache_hit with missing keytag. I have a rough count ~240 requests across 3 dev tokens in the QA org. Not prod tokens so far.

maria: confirmed: affected tokens are dev/test tokens only (we scoped the rewrap to dev kvring first). No evidence of prod tokens using the legacy cache key.

raj: mitigation plan:
- immediate: flip the feature-flag to disable cache-fallback (authz.fallback_to_tagless=false) so tagless fallback is blocked.
- short-term: purge authz cache entries created before 2026-03-18T02:00Z.
- medium: patch to make fallback validate per-route scope even when tag missing.
- long-term: ensure KMS rewrap triggers a cache invalidation hook.

sam: I'll flip the feature flag and purge the cache now, will update when done. Assigning myself 30m window to monitor.

sam: done — feature-flag flipped and purge job kicked off. Watching metrics. authz.cache.fallback_rate back to baseline.

maria: thanks. I'll open a PR for the strict validation on the fallback path (will include unit + integration test).

elaine: I'll run a full audit query across all environments to ensure no prod drift: query pattern `decision=allow AND route=/v1/embeddings AND auth_check IN (fallback,cache_hit) AND token_env!=prod`. Will share results in 30m.

raj: one more ask — what about audit logs and compliance? We need to tag these incidents and produce a short incident report for the SOC / compliance team. Security-bot, can you create SEC ticket and link audit artifacts?

security-bot: created ticket SEC-2026-45: "Authz cache tag fallback allowed dev-token route mismatch during KMS rewrap". Attached query: `authz_decision:allow AND route:/v1/embeddings AND timeframe:2026-03-18T01:50Z..2026-03-18T02:30Z`

tony: action owners:
- maria: PR for fallback validation (link when ready)
- raj: coordinate QA for the patch and help with integration tests
- elaine: full audit across envs + export csv of affected tokens and requests
- sam: monitor for 24h and confirm no prod bleed
- tony: schedule a short postmortem and notify CISO for visibility

maria: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/authz/pulls/842 (contains fix + tests). Requesting review from @raj and @elaine.

elaine: audit finished — 248 total requests from 5 dev tokens, all in the dev-qa namespace. CSV uploaded to secure drive: s3://redwood-secure/audit/SEC-2026-45/dev-token-audit.csv

raj: merging test + patch now, rolling to canary.

sam: canary looks good, no new allow anomalies in the last 45m. Metrics stable.

tony: thanks everyone. We'll keep this open until the postmortem is written and SOC confirms ticket closure.

maria: adding remediation note — we should also include an automated cache-invalidate hook in the KMS rewrap workflow so this class of issue is impossible to reoccur without a manual override.

security-bot: SEC-2026-45 status updated -> "triaged, remediation in progress"

raj: lesson: cache key shape changes are effectively a security boundary when they carry authz context. treat cache schema changes as breaking and force invalidation during rollout.

maria: agreed. will include this in the postmortem write-up. :memo:
